intro: From up here the Göksu valley lies at your command. You are at Silifke Castle, a castle and walls in Mersin province, from the 7th century. Through the crusades this castle was the key to Cilicia, and its ditch was cut straight into the rock.
history: The castle on this hill commanding the Göksu valley was founded under Byzantium. Through the crusades it was counted as the key to Cilicia. Look at its ditch: it is cut into the rock itself. Such a prize was fought over, and it changed hands repeatedly between the Knights Templar and the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the rock-cut ditch and the twenty-three towers, then the cistern and the Tekir cistern.
facts: Did you know? The Holy Roman Emperor Frederick Barbarossa drowned in 1190 in the Göksu below this castle, during the Third Crusade. Through the crusades the castle was counted as the key to Cilicia, changing hands repeatedly between the Templars and the Armenian kingdom.
outro: This brings our tour of Silifke Castle to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for climbing with us, and enjoy your visit.
